newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen pulling back after rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen pulling back after rally.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Coffee is likely to pull back after last week's rally, but another assault on the highs is possible in the longer term, technical analysts said on Monday.
Traders were looking for an open at around $10 higher.
"A bit of a weak close on Friday suggests it's seen the highs for the time being," independent analyst Elli Gifford said.
Nearby LIFFE robusta coffee futures widened losses in the London afternoon to end Friday sharply down as scale-up origin offers stalled the week's fund-led rally.
Gifford saw some support below $1,750 a tonne, with stronger support at $1,700. "in the longer term I suspect it's going to test $1,800 again. Whether it will break through it is another question."
New York coffee futures ended last week on a quiet note, finishing Friday mostly firmer as locals beefed up their positions ahead of the weekend, trading sources said.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified stocks increasing by 1,500 bags to 26,919 bags as of May 8. There were 16,615 bags of coffee pending grading.
Despite the modest certified stock build, traders said consumer coffee inventories were still extremely low.
They said continued supply worries, notably over Colombia, and the onset of the Brazilian winter should keep prices well underpinned.
Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were higher on Monday, despite declines in London, on the back of strong demand, traders said.

"Local prices are not decreasing, despite declines in London, because of strong demand and expectations of lower production this year," one trader said. "Players are now convinced output will be significantly lower this year."
The traders said they expected London's benchmark July contract to be $10-$20 higher when the market opens later.
